brewing.notes: A safe starting point for black tea: Western style, water just off the boil.

description:
A geographical-indication black tea from Xishui county in Zunyi, Guizhou, where the Dalou mountains drop to the edge of the Sichuan basin.

Treat it as you would any black tea: water just off the boil, a few minutes in the pot, and a seller who can say where it was grown.
history: China's former quality inspection authority granted it geographical-indication protection in May 2017, covering the whole county. Little is documented about its earlier history.
processing: Typical of black tea: withered, rolled, fully oxidised and dried.
harvest_season: Picked through the growing season, as with most black teas.
appearance_dry: Fine, tight, slightly curled leaves with visible tips, oily black.
taste_profile: Mellow with a sweet return, stands up to repeated steeping, with a rich floral-fruit or floral-honey aroma.
vintage_note: Black teas are normally sold by harvest year and are best within a couple of years.
